display.purpose: Brand wordmark, every panel/section title, every large stat number — not a single hero headline.

body.purpose: Paragraphs, descriptions, form values, everything not a title or a data value.

mono.purpose: Reference IDs, timestamps, tokens, API keys — anything read aloud or copy-pasted exactly.

shadows.name: toast-float
shadows.purpose: Bottom-center toast — the one confirmed exception to flat-by-default, used only because this element floats above the whole page.

shadows.name: flag-float
shadows.purpose: Top-right ambient notification — same floating-above-the-page justification as toast-float.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single loud, unmistakably-clickable action on a screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #F5A623; color: #1A1200; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F5A623; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Every non-primary action, including low-drama destructive ones.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #F5A623; font-weight: 500; font-size: 12px; padding: 7px 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #232F47; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #F5A62399; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F5A623; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge (position-gradient)
components.description: Signature component: color is computed from the status's position in the org's own ordered list (blue -> teal, early -> late), never from the status name itself, since statuses are fully org-configurable.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid; }

components.name: Exception Badge (tinted-badge recipe)
components.description: The same tinted recipe used for every escalation/practice/awaiting-approval exception badge, just with a different semantic color and label per case.
components.css: .ds-badge-exception { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 6px; background: #F0483E22; color: #F0483E; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Always one background step lighter than whatever panel contains it.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #182338; border: 1px solid #232F47; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 10px; font-size: 13px; color: #E8ECF3; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #8B96AB; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #F5A62399; } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Panel / Card
components.description: The atomic layout unit — a page is a vertical sequence of these. Flat, never shadowed.
components.html:
Time spent
Automatic, from status history.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: #121B2E; border: 1px solid #232F47; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; } .ds-panel-title { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; color: #E8ECF3; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-panel-body { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; color: #8B96AB; }

narrative.overview: Named by the author, not user-confirmed — the user declined all three offered North Star options without naming a replacement. Grounded in confirmed, evidence-backed logic: one hue (amber) is allowed to carry weight on any given screen, and every other color already has a specific, claimed meaning rather than existing for decoration. Confirmed mood: calm & restrained. Confirmed component character: tactile and confident. The system reads as a technical operations console: exact monospaced data sits next to plain-language copy, depth comes from stacked flat layers of near-black navy rather than shadow, and the whole thing stays legible and calm while someone is looking at it because something is actually wrong.
keyCharacteristics: One primary accent (amber), used sparingly, never decoratively
Fully flat — depth is layered background steps plus hairline borders, not shadows
Every non-neutral hue has one specific, claimed meaning; none are interchangeable
Monospace for anything a human reads aloud or copies; Inter for everything else

rules.name: The One Claimed Meaning Rule
rules.body: No hue is reused across two unrelated concepts on the same surface. Every existing color already means something specific; introducing a new use for an existing hue recreates a real, previously-shipped ambiguity bug.

rules.name: The Tinted Badge Rule
rules.body: Every status/severity/exception badge uses the same recipe: color+"22" background, color+"55" border, solid color text/icon. Never a solid-fill badge; never a plain-bordered one.

rules.name: The Read-Aloud Rule
rules.body: If a value is something a person might read aloud or copy-paste exactly (an ID, a token, a timestamp), it's set in JetBrains Mono. Everything else is Inter.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing embedded in the page lifts off it. A state that needs to stand out within the page gets a color wash and a colored border, never a shadow or a translate/scale hover lift — reserve an actual shadow for a transient element floating above the whole page (a toast, an ambient notification).

rules.name: The Position Gradient Rule
rules.body: Status color is a function of list position (blue to teal, early to late), never a string match on a status name — statuses are fully org-configurable.

dos: Do reserve Signal Amber for the single primary action or a genuinely high-severity/near-breach signal — never decoration.
Do use the Tinted Badge recipe for any new status/exception indicator, never a solid-fill or plain-outline badge.
Do set any ID, token, or timestamp in JetBrains Mono.
Do derive status/severity color from data (position in list, severity rank) rather than hardcoding to a label string.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow to anything embedded in the page — reserve it for a transient element that genuinely floats above the whole page.
Don't reuse an existing hue for a new, unrelated meaning — this project has already shipped and fixed the ambiguity bug that causes.
Don't set body text below Faint Slate (#838EA9) on either Deep Signal Navy or Console Panel — a real WCAG regression was found and fixed here before.
Don't hardcode a status or category name anywhere in styling logic — both are fully org-configurable per business template.
